response.sql:
WITH per_order_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    ordersmark,
    AVG(fillcount) as avg_fill
  FROM orderexecutions
  WHERE fillcount IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ordersmark
),
first_benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_fill) as first_avg
  FROM per_order_avg
),
filtered_first_pass AS (
  SELECT 
    poa.ordersmark,
    poa.avg_fill,
    poa.avg_fill - fb.first_avg as first_excess
  FROM per_order_avg poa
  CROSS JOIN first_benchmark fb
  WHERE poa.avg_fill > fb.first_avg
),
second_benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_fill) as second_avg
  FROM filtered_first_pass
),
filtered_second_pass AS (
  SELECT 
    ffp.avg_fill,
    ffp.first_excess,
    ffp.avg_fill - sb.second_avg as second_excess
  FROM filtered_first_pass ffp
  CROSS JOIN second_benchmark sb
  WHERE ffp.avg_fill > sb.second_avg
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_fill) as avg_fill_quantity,
  AVG(first_excess) as avg_first_excess,
  AVG(second_excess) as avg_second_excess
FROM filtered_second_pass;

assumptions.assumption: NULL values in fillcount should be excluded from per-order average calculations (only non-NULL fillcounts are averaged). The phrase 'ignore missing quantities' is interpreted as skipping NULL rows, not treating them as 0.

alternatives.interpretation: NULL values in fillcount should be treated as 0 when calculating per-order averages, based on the reading that 'ignore missing quantities' means to include them but count them as 0 fills.
